jamie-pm: Quick question — I need a 30d audit snapshot for a suspected permission change. Who can run ad-hoc exports and what format do we get? Need user_email redacted. Any approvals needed? cc @security-oncall :eyes:
ben-ops: You need the `audit_exporter` role to run exports. If you don't have it, ping Eng Security. We default to Parquet for size/perf, but can do JSONL if you need line-delimited records for tooling.
ben-ops: Quick workflow: 1) Open infra-requests ticket with incident link 2) tag `security-review` 3) specify TTL for the S3 link (default 7d). We follow the `audit_logs_export` playbook.
ben-ops: Example (internal tool):
```
./tools/export_audit.sh --days 30 --format parquet --redact=user_email
```
security-oncall-bot: Policy note: exports are redacted by default (policy v2.0). If you need raw emails/PII, that requires Security Manager + Legal approval — documented in /docs/security/export-approvals.md.
niki: How is redaction applied? Is it done during the export job or after the file is written? I need ETA implications for the incident timeline.
ben-ops: Redaction happens server-side as part of the export job (before writing to S3). We replace `user_email` with a hashed id and drop fields flagged PII. That adds ~5-10% CPU, so expect slightly longer runtime.
vikram: Note for Dedicated customers: we mirror exports to customer-owned S3 buckets and retention is set by contract. If this snapshot is for a customer, loop in the account team.
jamie-pm: Thanks — opened infra-requests/1234 and tagged security-review. Requested TTL=3d. Assigning to @ben-ops to run when available.
ben-ops: Got it, I'll run the export tomorrow AM and paste the presigned S3 link here when done. :thumbsup:
security-oncall-bot: Export job queued (job id: j-98765). ETA ~4h. The generated S3 link will include `expires_at` metadata and the ticket id in the path.
